title: Flat maps that are isomorphisms modulo I are isomorphisms modulo all powers of I
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal; write $I^nB$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by $\varphi(I^n)$. Assume that the ring map $A/I\to B/IB$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Then for every $n\ge1$ the ring map $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, line 3105): 'Since each $A\to B$ is flat we find that the maps $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ are isomorphisms as well (for example by Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-lift-basis})', i.e. Algebra Lemma Tag 051H (lemma-lift-basis, algebra.tex line 24343) applied to $R=A/I^n$, the nilpotent ideal $I/I^n$, $M=B/I^nB$ and the single element $1$ (Tor-vanishing by flatness of $B$ over $A$)

proof.text: Equip B with the A-algebra structure induced by φ. Surjectivity of β₁ gives surjectivity of A → B/IB. Induct on n, starting with the zero quotient for n=0. Given a lift modulo I^n, Mathlib AdicCompletion.exists_smodEq_pow_smul_top_and_mkQ_eq corrects it modulo I^(n+1). Ideal.smul_top_eq_map identifies module quotients with the ring quotients, proving surjectivity of every βₙ. This is the coefficient-lifting argument of Algebra 051H, implemented in the private helper surjective_mkQ_pow.

For J = I^n, the quotient tensor equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], in its swapped form Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor, identifies B/JB with (A/J) tensor_A B as an A/J-algebra. Module.Flat.baseChange and Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv give flatness of βₙ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The private helper flat_quotientMap implements this argument.

For n ≥ 1, I^n ≤ I. If βₙ(a mod I^n)=0, then φ(a) belongs to IB; injectivity of β₁ implies a belongs to I. Thus ker βₙ is contained in the image of I in A/I^n. Its nth power is zero, since Ideal.map_pow identifies that power with the image of I^n. Hence ker βₙ is nilpotent.

For a surjective flat ring map f, the first isomorphism theorem identifies R/ker(f) with its flat target. Thus ker(f) is pure. Mathlib Ideal.isIdempotentElem_of_pure makes it idempotent; IsIdempotentElem.pow_succ_eq shows every positive power equals it. Nilpotence forces it to be zero (the exponent-zero case forces the entire ring to be zero). RingHom.injective_iff_ker_eq_bot gives injectivity. Apply this proved private helper injective_of_flat_surjective_nilpotent_ker to βₙ and combine with its surjectivity. No short five lemma or graded-piece maps are needed.
